reference: No matching GNU DHCP client/parser CLI is available for bashdhcp parse-message, so runnable operation cases are honest contract checks, not GNU parity. Their packets are encoded independently from the BOOTP fixed-header layout and RFC 2131/2132 DHCP option codes; expected values are derived from the encoded fields. The metadata case uses the builtin help text documented by the bashdhcp registration. Network operations are deferred to explicit isolated-peer fixtures.
coverage: Bash builtin type/help metadata and documented request/renew/release/parse-message forms.

DHCP OFFER parsing: yiaddr, siaddr, subnet mask, first router, complete DNS/NTP lists, domain, server ID, lease/renew times, option-66 TFTP server, and option-67 bootfile overriding the BOOTP file field.
Documented -V associative-array binding for ip, netmask, gateway, dns, domain, server_id, lease_time, and renew_time.
Short packet, truncated DHCP option, and invalid hexadecimal rejection.
Deferred request, renew, release, and inform exchange behavior requiring an isolated mock peer.
exclusions: No GNU parity is claimed because there is no matching GNU CLI for the parser API.
No DHCP packet is sent on the host or test runner; request/renew/release/inform require future disposable VM and isolated mock fixtures.
No interface discovery, socket binding, or privilege behavior is asserted by the parser contracts.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports the statically available builtin and exposes the documented DHCPv4 usage text through help.
cases.stdout:
type=builtin
bashdhcp: DHCPv4 client (RFC2131 DISCOVER/OFFER/REQUEST/ACK + parse-message)
    DHCPv4 client and message parser.
    
        bashdhcp request -i IFACE [-h LEASE_VAR] [-t TIMEOUT_MS]
        bashdhcp renew   -i IFACE [-h LEASE_VAR]
        bashdhcp release -i IFACE LEASE
        bashdhcp parse-message HEX [-V VAR]
    
    LEASE_VAR is an associative array with ip/netmask/gateway/dns/domain/server_id/lease_time/renew_time.

cases.purpose: Check that a decoded packet shorter than the fixed BOOTP header is rejected with command failure and no parsed output.
cases.script:
if bashdhcp parse-message 00; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%d\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Check the option-length boundary: encode a 236-byte BOOTP header and valid cookie followed by an option declaring one missing value byte.
cases.script:
packet=
for ((i=0; i<236; i++)); do packet+=00; done
packet+=638253633501
if bashdhcp parse-message "$packet"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%d\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: Check that non-hexadecimal input is rejected as a usage error and produces no parsed output.
cases.script:
if bashdhcp parse-message 12xz; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%d\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc -eq 2 ]]

cases.purpose: Validate the complete DHCP client acquisition exchange and returned lease against a private peer.
cases.reason: Only the offline parser is executed. The live request path is reachable on loopback today: BASHDHCP_SERVER_ADDR/BASHDHCP_SERVER_PORT/BASHDHCP_CLIENT_PORT redirect it, and SO_BINDTODEVICE works as VM root with -i lo. What is missing is a DHCP-aware peer.

cases.purpose: Validate DHCP renewal packet fields and ACK handling using an isolated configured interface.
cases.reason: renew is reachable on loopback (server_id 127.0.0.1 + BASHDHCP_SERVER_PORT/CLIENT_PORT, -i lo); a DHCP-aware peer is missing.

cases.purpose: Validate that release emits a DHCPRELEASE with the lease address and server identifier to the intended isolated peer.
cases.reason: release is reachable on loopback (lease server_id=127.0.0.1, BASHDHCP_SERVER_PORT, -i lo as root); the existing udp peer captures raw bytes but the random xid prevents byte comparison, so a decoding peer record is needed.

cases.purpose: Validate DHCPINFORM construction and option-bearing ACK decoding on a private link.
cases.reason: inform hard-codes UDP port 67 and limited broadcast (bashdhcp.c:590) and binds no client port, so it needs a script-built private veth topology rather than the loopback peer; no fixture exists.
